hook.text: During COVID, Italy's hospitals ran out of ventilators. Doctors had to decide who received life support and who did not.

buildup.text: Age-based cutoffs were proposed. Over 80, no ventilator. This saved more life-years but felt like age discrimination.

discovery.text: Most hospitals used survival probability instead. The patient most likely to survive with treatment gets the ventilator.

twist.text: Survival probability still correlates with age and health conditions that track with race and poverty.

climax.text: Pandemic triage shows that no allocation rule is morally clean. Every framework saves some lives and sacrifices others.

punchline.text: Save whom? Every rule helps some and harms others.

quiz.question: Why is pandemic triage ethically complex?
options: Every allocation framework saves some lives at the cost of others with no neutral option
